name: Emmforce Autotech Limited
summary: Emmforce is an export-focused precision drivetrain manufacturer moving from aftermarket batches into a large US OEM programme and an 80%-owned agri/forging ramp. FY26 group revenue rose 28.68% to ₹112.65 crore but PAT only 2.27% to ₹8.25 crore. Cash conversion and incremental capital returns remain weak. More importantly, the consolidated reserves, earnings, NCI and goodwill bridge is unresolved. At ₹192.50 on 19 October 2026, equity value is ₹394.62 crore, approximately 47.85 times reported PAT. BQS, GQS (Growth Quality) and IAS are NS. CAP lacks a defensible multi-year incremental-return or mature cohort basis. BQS coverage is 88%, bounds 4.36–5.44; GQS coverage 85%, bounds 4.75–6.10. IAS coverage is 40%, canonical bounds 1.80–7.20, tightened to 2.64–6.06 when nested quality bounds are propagated. Classification: Watchlist, with financial-reliability and funding holds; a manufacturing capacity-ramp special situation, not a validated compounder. Missing CAP makes quality scores incomplete. Independently, G2 affects core owner-earnings reliability and also prevents ranking. Funding Hold alone would not exclude BQS/GQS rankings.

score_note: CAP NS prevents BQS/GQS point scores: coverage88%/85%, bounds4.36–5.44/4.75–6.10. IAS Q and R missing: coverage40%, canonical bounds1.80–7.20, tighter nested bounds2.64–6.06. No numerical overrides. G2 independently excludes rankings; G3 Hold alone does not exclude quality.

gates.reason: Reporting and stewardship weaknesses support GOV 4; an unmodified audit is contrary evidence. No verified severe-integrity failure.
Material goodwill, reserves, PAT and NCI bridge remains unresolved, affecting owner-earnings reliability.
Annual paths have early cash gaps without new money; unused committed bank headroom is unverified. Authorization ceilings are not funding. No actual default or G3 Fail is inferred.
Current dated eligible series and lot verified. Only 59 of 60 secondary sessions, whole-lot constraints and unverified live BSE restrictions prevent full execution clearance.

GOV.reason: Material facts are the FY26 consolidated earnings/reserves/goodwill inconsistency and the revised FY24 period comparators. Significant promoter-linked sales, procurement and subsidiary funding increase the need for minority-shareholder scrutiny. Contrary evidence: unmodified audit, disclosed transactions and approval processes; no verified diversion, current default or fraud. Score 4 reflects reporting/stewardship weakness, not a severe-integrity override.

MOAT.reason: Precision high-mix components, machining/forging integration and customer validation create moderate switching friction; actual OEM commercialization is stronger evidence than a sector growth story. Contrary: the largest customer is 47%, top ten 93%, historical destocking is material and Sona/Talbros/RACL demonstrate capable competition. Pricing power, lifetime customer economics and defensible market share are ND. Mixed moat, score 5.

REV.reason: The five-year comparable predecessor/standalone goods-plus-jobwork CAGR of 14.6935% gives scheduled REV 6, with no discretionary adjustment. FY26 comparable standalone commercial growth of 19.60% and group reported growth of 28.68% are positives. Contrary: FY23 destocking inflates three-year recovery CAGR; the short FY24 comparator and FX/incentive reclassification can overstate growth. Ten-year history and complete price/volume attribution are ND.

DUR.reason: Installed lines and the commercial multi-year US programme provide accessible runway; agri/forging products could diversify demand. Contrary: customer concentration, unknown cancellation terms, low agri utilization and substantial cash needs constrain capture. The ₹350 crore capacity estimate and ₹470 crore order are management claims, not funded or guaranteed sales. Score 6 balances tangible capacity with execution constraints.

CAP.reason: NS: the one-year incremental ROIC diagnostic is 4.85%, or 5.40% excluding goodwill, but it is not a meaningful three-/five-year capital-return window or mature unit/cohort substitute. Corporate conversion, subsidiary investment/eliminations, a late commissioning ramp and the unresolved consolidation bridge prevent an attributable comparable economic-capital series. Average ROIC of 8.96% and ₹57.96 crore of cash capex are useful warnings, not proof of additional-capital returns. Contrary positive evidence: installed capacity and commercial production could improve returns as investments mature. Missing incremental-return evidence is distinct from a demonstrated poor CAP score and from G2 reliability.

CASH.reason: Two comparable years give CFO/PAT of 16.64%, FY26 FCF of negative ₹18.18 crore and substantial inventory/receivables absorption. Positive contrary evidence is CFO recovery to ₹5.25 crore and fewer debtors older than six months. The two-year ramp and perimeter break do not establish a persistent three-to-five-year failure, so no CASH cap applies. Three/five-year conversion is ND. Score 4.

BAL.reason: Reported cash of ₹0.45 crore including FDs is thin against ₹5.29 crore current maturities, ₹18.58 crore WC borrowing and modeled ramp funding gaps. Contrary: net debt/operating EBITDA is 1.92 times, interest coverage 5.57 times, book equity positive and no current default verified. Subsidiary loan/guarantee ceilings are not available funding. Score 4 and funding Hold, not demonstrated survival failure.

EXEC.reason: Commercial US production, actual plant commissioning and FY26 revenue within the earlier ₹100–125 crore outlook are positives. Contrary: the initial September 2025 start moved to December production and March material revenue, while the subsidiary remained loss-making. Score 5 records mixed execution. Future ₹195/240 crore guidance is not achievement.

EARN.reason: Group PAT grew only 2.27% versus revenue 28.68%; PAT margin fell to 7.32%, depreciation almost doubled and subsidiary losses diluted parent growth. Contrary: operating EBITDA rose 34.45%, parent PAT 13.78%, and FX-neutral EBITDA improved. Lower investment income and higher depreciation explain part of the divergence, but owner EPS/NCI remains unreconciled. Score 4.

R.reason: NS. A supported investable base return cannot be established while material consolidation reconciliation and committed funding are missing. The 7.83% unfunded base diagnostic and 7.57% hypothetically bridged case are sensitivities, not a scoreable investment base. Do not map an unsupported IRR to an integer or compensate with an arbitrary penalty.

D.reason: Bear terminal value of ₹48.39 implies 74.86% price loss before friction; its ₹17.97 crore buffer deficit and the linked stress gap of ₹38.42 crore show material recapitalization risk. Contrary: productive facilities, profitable parent operations and interest coverage offer recovery potential; no actual insolvency is established. Score 3 measures loss severity, not a duplicate penalty for the unscored expected return.

P.reason: Approximately 47.85 times reported PAT and 19.32 times operating EBITDA require several optimistic assumptions together. At 11-times exit EBITDA and 22% margin, fixed-financing algebra needs about ₹353.46 crore commercial sales for the 15% hurdle, versus ₹108.31 crore today. Seven-times normalization turns the base diagnostic negative. Contrary: installed capacity and a commercial programme offer a route to growth. Score 3, not a claim that all growth is impossible.

L.reason: Twenty complete recent observations, 59 of 60 longer-window observations and explicit missing-row turnover bounds imply 3.82–4.04 continuous exit days at 5%, starting score 7. The verified 1,200-share lot costs ₹2.31 lakh; only 9 of 59 observed sessions can absorb a whole lot at 5%. Two-lot known capacity is approximately 10.91 sessions, with completed-start median 11. Explicit downgrade to 3 for lumpy implementation. Contrary: recent 20-session capacity is better and SM eligibility verified. Restrictions/spread remain ND; conditional historical grade, not execution clearance.

derived_tighter_bounds.method: Propagate BQS bounds 4.36–5.44 into Q at 25%, then R from 1 to 10 at 35%, plus known D/P/L contribution 1.20. Canonical missing-factor schedule remains 1.80–7.20.

ranking_eligibility.reason: CAP is unscoreable, making both quality aggregates incomplete. Independently, G2 affects core consolidated capital and owner earnings. IAS also lacks Q and a supported R. This is not automatic exclusion for SME status or G3 funding Hold.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Emmforce is an export-focused precision drivetrain manufacturer moving from aftermarket batches into a large US OEM programme and an 80%-owned agri/forging ramp. FY26 group revenue rose 28.68% to ₹112.65 crore but PAT only 2.27% to ₹8.25 crore. Cash conversion and incremental capital returns remain weak. More importantly, the consolidated reserves, earnings, NCI and goodwill bridge is unresolved. [S1,S6]

At ₹192.50 on 19 October 2026, equity value is ₹394.62 crore, approximately 47.85 times reported PAT. BQS, GQS (Growth Quality) and IAS are NS. CAP lacks a defensible multi-year incremental-return or mature cohort basis. BQS coverage is 88%, bounds 4.36–5.44; GQS coverage 85%, bounds 4.75–6.10. IAS coverage is 40%, canonical bounds 1.80–7.20, tightened to 2.64–6.06 when nested quality bounds are propagated. Classification: Watchlist, with financial-reliability and funding holds; not a validated compounder. Missing CAP makes quality scores incomplete. Independently, G2 affects core owner-earnings reliability and also prevents ranking. Funding Hold alone would not exclude BQS/GQS rankings. [S1,S14,S16]

The potential advantage is customer-approved engineering plus installed capacity, not a proven brand or protected market share. The central bear path is OEM/agri ramp disappointment while inventory, debt and subsidiary losses consume cash. A low-capex earnings recovery is possible, but cannot be accepted without a reconciled consolidation pack and bank-headroom evidence. Historical figures and conditional model diagnostics are useful; none is a completed, financed investment return case. [S1,S6,S9]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Emmforce Autotech Limited, BSE SME 544166, ISIN INE0SDC01012. The interoperable exchange master identifies the eligible SM line as EMMFORCE$. Original listing: 30 April 2024. The predecessor business operated before corporate conversion on 13 October 2023; marketing references to broader group history are not the issuer's legal age. [S1,S3,S14]

Research cutoff: 20 October 2026. Sources were retrieved on 21 October, but only documents and price observations dated at or before cutoff are admitted. Dated secondary close: ₹192.50 on 19 October; 20,499,600 issued shares; market capitalization ₹394.6173 crore. No share split or bonus is inferred from a price chart. Current share count is distinct from historical EPS weighted-average shares. Reference cases assume no dilution; a separate equity-raising sensitivity changes both cash and diluted shares. [S1,S14,S16]

G1 Integrity: Conditional. Reporting and stewardship concerns support GOV 4, not a severe-integrity failure or fraud allegation. G2 Reliability: Hold. The economically material reserves/PAT/NCI/goodwill inconsistency prevents a reliable owner-earnings bridge. G3 Funding: Hold, not established. Prospective cash gaps exist without additional financing, but unused sanctioned limits, expiry and renewal terms are not quantified. This is not proof of actual default or an automatic IAS cap. G4 Tradability: Conditional. Eligible line and lot are verified, but current BSE surveillance, live bid-ask depth and complete official company trading history are not. [S1,S6,S14,S18]

Financial statements use the issuer's Accounting Standards presentation under Section 133; no unverified Ind AS conversion is imposed. The nominal, pre-personal-tax investment horizon is exactly 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031. Equity hurdle: 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. Return annualization uses actual days divided by 365.2425, giving a 4.999418 year fraction for the exact five-calendar-year anniversary. Fiscal funding diagnostics start from the last verified 31 March 2026 balance sheet and extend FY27–FY32; terminal operating run rate and financial balances are interpolated to 19 October 2031. Actual interim FY27 cash/debt at entry is ND. Analytical capital-cost range: 11–14%, not a claimed company WACC. Liquidity reference: ₹5 lakh, not an allocation recommendation. Identity confidence is High; filed operating data Medium; consolidation and owner earnings Low; arithmetic High but forecasts Low. Overall confidence Low and forecast uncertainty High. [S1,S3,S16]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factor scores: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 4; R NS, D 3, P 3, L 3. Each audit records supporting facts and contrary evidence. No missing factor receives a neutral score. [E1–E13]

BQS known contributions are 0.80 + 1.00 + 0.72 + 0.60 + missing CAP + 0.40 + 0.32 + 0.40 = 4.24. CAP has 12% weight, so coverage is 88% and mathematical completion bounds are 4.36–5.44. GQS known contributions are 2.40 + 1.20 + 0.60 + missing CAP + 0.40 = 4.60. Missing weight is 15%, coverage 85%, bounds 4.75–6.10. Both raw/final scores remain NS. No midpoint or renormalization is supplied. Rounded interval displays are 4.4–5.4 and 4.8–6.1; exact bounds control interpretation. [model/score_audit.txt]

IAS inherits missing Q because BQS is NS, and independently lacks supported R. Known D/P/L contributions total 0.60 + 0.30 + 0.30 = 1.20. Coverage is 40%, missing weight 60%, canonical factor-completion bounds 1.80–7.20. Applying the tighter BQS bounds within Q gives a separate nested interval of 2.64–6.06. IAS remains NS under either representation. GQS is not added into IAS. Unknown CAP is not a demonstrated poor-return score: the one-year proxy and current ROIC cannot replace a meaningful multi-year or cohort return test. [model/score_audit.txt]

No caps apply. GOV 4 does not trigger GOV ≤3; CAP is unknown, not persistently ≤3; CASH 4 does not trigger a persistent cash-failure cap. All ranking flags are false because quality aggregates are incomplete and, separately, G2 affects core financial reliability. Funding Hold alone or the SME label does not automatically exclude quality. L 3 is a whole-lot downgrade from continuous-capacity starting 7, not an unknown-data placeholder. Sensitivity to MOAT and DUR each moving one point gives BQS bounds 4.06–5.74; DUR and EARN each moving one point give GQS 4.40–6.45. These are mathematical sensitivities, not statistical confidence intervals or precise rankings. [E4,E6,E12]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The issuer manufactures precision drivetrain parts including axle shafts, differential components, hubs/spindles and related tooling for overseas aftermarket, performance/off-road and newer OEM customers. Its Baddi manufacturing system combines development, machining, metallurgy, quality validation and forging access. It is a manufacturing business, not an asset-light royalty stream. Repeat orders and engineering approvals support relationships, while end demand remains tied to customer inventory, vehicle/off-road use, replacement demand and model programmes. [S1,S3]

Emmforce Mobility Solutions Private Limited is the 80%-owned subsidiary. It is not synonymous with the listed parent or the broader promoter Emmbros group. It supplies forging/agri components and is scaling rotavator, blade and tractor applications. FY26 subsidiary turnover was ₹12.1435 crore, loss ₹3.7577 crore and net worth negative ₹2.42145 crore. Its assets were ₹36.9000 crore and liabilities ₹39.3215 crore. [S1:p91]

Parent standalone FY26 sales of ₹104.4683 crore and PAT ₹12.0633 crore cannot substitute for consolidated sales ₹112.6458 crore and PAT ₹8.2478 crore. Parent plus subsidiary sales total ₹116.6119 crore, implying ₹3.9660 crore of consolidation eliminations; the detailed intercompany profit/tax bridge is not fully disclosed. [S1:pp114,140,91]

FY26 group goods exports of ₹102.1214 crore represent 94.29% of goods-plus-jobwork commercial sales of ₹108.3090 crore. Reported operating revenue also includes foreign exchange gains and export incentives. Domestic agri operations could diversify the business but have not yet demonstrated material group profit. Broader family manufacturing experience does not entitle listed shareholders to all group brands, assets, sales or potential merger economics. [S1:p147]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The moat mechanism is moderate engineering and validation friction. High-mix components require drawings, tooling, tolerances, metallurgy and delivery reliability. A validated programme cannot always change suppliers overnight. Installed forging and automation can reduce outsourcing and improve response times. Commercialization of the US line is evidence of customer acceptance, stronger than a generic market-size claim. Nevertheless, aftermarket buyers can multisource; pricing power, retention rates and issuer market share are not independently established. [S3,S6,S9]

Concentration is important contrary evidence. The presentation's top 1/3/5/10 customer shares were 52/76/84/92% in FY24, 46/65/75/89% in FY25, and 47/71/83/93% in H1FY26. Diversification has not persisted across the latest window. The prospectus's FY23 North America share of 77.38% is historical, not a current country mix. Current export dependence and the US programme imply currency, logistics, trade-policy and customer inventory risk. No unverified current tariff rate is asserted. Prospeedways related-party sales may overlap the largest customer exposures; the percentages must not be added as independent risks. [S1,S3:p121,S8:p12]

Three primary-source comparators establish boundaries rather than an unmatched P/E average. Sona Comstar has much broader global OEM and precision driveline capabilities; its FY25 annual report cites 8.8% differential-gear share for CY2024, a stronger-scale benchmark rather than Emmforce market-share evidence. Talbros Engineering supplies integrated axle forging, heat treatment and machining across vehicle/agri applications, an overlapping product/process competitor. RACL Geartech's precision gears and shafts show that engineering capability is not unique. Their scale, end-market mix, EV exposure, capital intensity, financial reporting and liquidity differ. Matched cutoff peer multiples are ND; no peer's historical multiple is relabeled as Emmforce fair value. MOAT 5 recognizes switching friction without claiming dominance. [S19,S20,S21]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Predecessor commercial revenue, ₹ crore: FY21 50.4517, FY22 69.0629, FY23 45.6908. Corporate conversion in October 2023 creates a perimeter break. Revised full-year FY24 combined predecessor/company revenue was 81.3307 consolidated and 81.2868 standalone, unlike later short corporate-period comparators. The approximately ₹40 crore short FY24 comparator must not generate a claim of 118% FY25 organic growth. Relative to revised full-year group revenue, FY25 reported 87.5405 grew 7.63%, subject to classification and perimeter caveats. FY26 group revenue 112.6458 grew 28.68%; standalone 104.4683 versus 87.4337 grew 19.48%. [S1,S3,S4,S5,S24]

There is also a classification break. FY21–FY23 prospectus revenue comprises domestic and export goods; forex gains and export incentives were other income. FY25–FY26 operating revenue includes these items. A consistent current standalone goods-plus-jobwork series is ₹83.7193 crore in FY25 and ₹100.1315 crore in FY26. Against FY21 ₹50.4517 crore, five-year CAGR is 14.6935%, giving REV starting score 6. Unadjusted FY26 revenue would inflate CAGR to 15.6703% and cross a scoring threshold. The three-year commercial CAGR from FY23 is 29.8915%, disclosed but not preferred because FY23 was a destocking trough. Ten-year growth is ND. Same-basis FY26 standalone growth is 19.60%; group commercial revenue ₹108.3090 versus ₹83.8260 grew 29.21%, including the subsidiary ramp. [S1:p147,S3:p179]

The prospectus explains excessive customer inventory during FY22 and destocking in FY23. FY21 also benefited from unusually strong pandemic orders, so this is not a smooth compounding history. Current growth drivers are the OEM ramp, new products/agri and utilization, not demonstrated price increases. A full annual price/volume/currency/acquisition bridge is ND. FY26 forex gains of ₹2.0816 crore and duty/RODTEP income of ₹2.2553 crore are separately identified, not mistaken for unit growth. The preferred five-year history and mixed current ramp justify no discretionary +1 trajectory adjustment. [S3:pp194–195,S1]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The physical option exists. Management estimates annual revenue capacity of roughly ₹200 crore in auto components and ₹150 crore in agri, with utilization of 50–55% and 8–10% respectively. These are management revenue-capacity estimates, not independently tested machine hours or additive consolidated TAM. Intercompany forging cannot be sold twice in a group model. The ₹470 crore US programme over nine years was announced in December 2024; the later “over ₹500 crore” order book includes it, not an additional ₹500 crore. Signed cancellation rights, take-or-pay provisions, unit prices and margin protection are ND. A headline order is not a receivable or cash. [S6:pp3–5,S7:pp14,16]

Management's FY27 outlook is ₹165 crore auto plus ₹30 crore agri, totaling ₹195 crore, followed by ₹240 crore in FY28 including ₹50 crore agri. Targets of 20–22% EBITDA and roughly 10% PAT margins remain claims. The US programme is expected to contribute about ₹60 crore annually after ₹5.5–6 crore of March 2026 sales. TAFE-related rotavator parts and blade products started at different times. No FY27 market share or complete guidance is banked. PPAP work, hydraulic-pump field trials and RFQs are opportunities, not contracted consolidated revenue. The August AGM did not provide quantified new half-year financial results. [S6:pp5,12–15,S8,S10]

Cash capex in FY25 and FY26 totaled ₹57.9648 crore. Group PPE plus CWIP rose ₹15.1413 crore in FY26, versus capex less depreciation of ₹15.2887 crore. The ₹0.1474 crore difference closely matches disposal/subsidy proceeds and the disposal loss; it is not wholly unexplained investment. But financing invested capital rose ₹29.5593 crore while normalized 26%-tax NOPAT rose ₹1.4338 crore. The one-year incremental ROIC proxy is 4.8507%, or 5.3999% excluding the goodwill increase. Average ROIC is 8.9604% and ROCE 12.1086% using consistent average invested capital, below or around the analytical 11–14% capital-cost range. The issuer's 13.05% ROCE uses a different published denominator and is not copied uncritically. Late commissioning and startup costs make this a lagged proxy, not mature project economics. Sustained incremental returns remain unproven. Three-/five-year group proxies are NM without a comparable capital/perimeter and attributable-profit bridge, while mature unit/cohort returns are ND. The one-year proxy cannot determine CAP. CAP and GQS therefore remain NS, with no persistent CAP/CASH override. Missing evidence is distinct from the G2 reliability issue. [S1:pp139–147;E6]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Ashok and Neetu Mehta are key promoter-directors. FY26 promoter-group rows total 15,272,400 shares, approximately 74.50%, versus roughly 73.17% previously. The directors' FY-end pledge statements are positive; latest cutoff encumbrances were not independently cleared. No FY26 ESOP, warrant, bonus or fresh share issue was identified. The IPO was entirely fresh: 5,499,600 shares at ₹98, gross ₹53.89608 crore less ₹4.01673 crore issue costs, giving ₹49.87935 crore net proceeds. This money is already in the FY25 cash bridge, not future funding. The November 2024 utilization statement reported no deviation but is not a complete current funds-tracing certificate. [S1:p142,S13]

The parent loan to the subsidiary of ₹28.72365 crore and equity investment of ₹3.2 crore are eliminated in consolidation. The existing ₹10 crore subsidiary guarantee is not another ₹10 crore of debt on top of the same consolidated bank borrowing. Proposed ₹35 crore loan and ₹25 crore guarantee/security ceilings are authorizations, not cash received or incremental committed bank limits. Outside the consolidated group, Prospeedways sales were ₹20.64284 crore, Emmbros Automotive goods purchases ₹14.02548 crore and machinery purchases ₹1.07232 crore. Management asserts arm's-length pricing; independent benchmarks and a full related-customer collection bridge are ND. Managerial remuneration of ₹1.97689 crore is approximately 24% of reported group PAT, a stewardship consideration but not automatically improper. [S1:pp71–72,154–155]

Promise versus delivery: original US programme production target September 2025; formal production commenced 16 December 2025; management says first material revenue arrived in March 2026 after customer clearance. Commercialization is real but delayed, not nine years of assured profit. FY26 sales of ₹112.65 crore met the prior ₹100–125 crore range; the agri subsidiary still lost ₹3.76 crore. Broader group merger discussion has no verified consideration, completion or financing, so no value is added. [S6,S7,S9]

The unmodified statutory audit, reported adequate controls and audit trail, and absence of an auditor-reported fraud/default finding are important contrary evidence. Revised FY24 presentation and the FY26 consolidation bridge nevertheless support GOV 4 and G2 Hold. The February 2025 protective GST refund notice involved approximately ₹0.3687071 crore principal reportedly already reversed/paid. Final disposal, interest and penalty were not verified. The annual nil-contingency statement is not proof that every historical procedural issue has vanished. No allegation of fraud, diversion or lender non-cooperation is made. [S1,S4,S12,S23,S24]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Consolidated FY25 → FY26, ₹ crore: revenue 87.5405 → 112.6458; other income 1.4862 → 0.0726; PBT 11.6839 → 12.0093; finance cost 2.4123 → 2.6108; depreciation 4.2654 → 8.1419; PAT 8.0649 → 8.2478. Operating EBITDA, defined as PBT + finance cost + depreciation − other income, rose from 16.8754 to 22.6895, or 34.45%. FX-neutral EBITDA rose from 15.3042 to 20.6079. PAT margin fell from 9.21% to 7.32%, while reported EPS moved from 3.93 to 4.02. Lower investment income after IPO cash deployment and higher depreciation explain much of the profit lag, but do not turn it into cash growth. An illustrative 26%-tax adjustment removing other income and forex gains reduces FY26 PAT by ₹1.5941 crore; it is not an accepted owner-earnings figure because consolidation is unresolved. [S1:pp140–148]

Consolidation control test: reserves increased ₹12.0573364 crore, all shown as profit addition, versus consolidated PAT ₹8.2477587 crore. NCI changed by negative ₹0.7515433 crore, matching 20% of the subsidiary loss of ₹3.7577166 crore. If this allocation is applied diagnostically, owner profit would be ₹8.9993020 crore, still ₹3.0580344 crore below the retained-profit addition. Goodwill increased ₹3.0061732 crore, essentially 80% of the same subsidiary loss; no FY26 ownership increase or new acquisition cash flow was identified. Parent PAT plus subsidiary PAT equals ₹8.3056013 crore, ₹0.0578426 crore above consolidated PAT, requiring an intercompany/tax elimination bridge. The reported EPS note calls the full ₹8.2478 crore attributable to equity shareholders without an NCI profit-allocation line. Prior-year reserve profit addition of ₹10.72865 crore also exceeds consolidated PAT ₹8.06492 crore. These are arithmetic inconsistencies, not proof of their cause or an accounting offence. The May call did not provide a reconciliation. G2 reopening requires acquisition-date values, ownership history, goodwill rollforward, NCI allocation and elimination entries, not merely another clean audit statement. [S1:pp139–142,155,91;S6:p17]

FY26 operating cash bridge: PBT 12.0093 + depreciation 8.1419 − investment income 0.0725 + interest 2.6108 + disposal loss 0.0022 + noncash adjustments 0.0519 − trade/other receivables 5.4997 − inventory 9.1289 + trade/other payables 3.4778 = cash generated 11.5929. Interest paid 2.6108 and tax 3.7326 leave CFO 5.2495. Working capital and tax, not capex, explain weak CFO. Investing outflow 23.5030 and financing inflow 9.1760 reduce reported cash from 9.5284 to 0.4509. CFO less cash capex is negative 18.1811 in FY26 and negative 37.0699 in FY25. Two comparable years give CFO 2.7138 / PAT 16.3127 = 16.6361% conversion. Three- and five-year group conversion are ND. FY24 corporate cash flow starts from a reset acquisition/conversion perimeter while full-year P&L combines the predecessor; prospectus interest was classified in financing rather than current CFO. Predecessor FY21/FY22/FY23 CFO of 7.1994/−0.8770/8.8675 is shown separately, not stitched into group cash conversion. [S1:p141,S3:p160,S5:p86]

Working capital: receivables 27.8427 → 33.6835, inventory 13.0522 → 22.1811, and trade payables 8.2363 → 11.4610. Average DSO is 99.68 days; closing DSO is 109.14 days. They are different measures. Receivables older than six months declined from 0.8095 to 0.5662, a positive, although balances remain subject to confirmation/reconciliation. WIP rose from 2.1705 to 5.2960 and finished goods from 1.9553 to 5.8154, tying profit and cash into the ramp. Future obsolescence is a risk, not an already-proven write-off. GST recoverable of 11.1205 and duty claims of 0.5873 are operating cash claims, not cash equivalents. Capital creditors 1.0640 and capital advances 0.1256 are separated from ordinary operating WC; income-tax assets/provisions are netted only in the opening settlement bridge, with no invented cash refund. [S1:pp144–147]

Debt of 44.1140 includes short-term borrowings of 23.8658, comprising 5.2899 of current maturities and 18.5759 of bank WC. Current maturities are not added twice. Promoter loans of 8.6606 remain external group debt. Reported cash 0.4509 includes FDs/margin money. The conservative reference cash balance of 0.08638 excludes all FDs and accrued interest; reported cash is separately tested as an availability sensitivity. Net debt/operating EBITDA is 1.924 times and EBIT/finance cost 5.572 times, but the cash buffer is thin. No additional off-balance-sheet third-party guaranteed debt was independently established beyond the subsidiary facility, and no lease liability is invented under the AS presentation. Customer credit, inventory realization, taxation and impairment remain forward risks. [S1:pp139,143–146]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the dated ₹192.50 close, equity value is ₹394.6173 crore. Reported net debt of ₹43.6631 crore gives EV ₹438.2804 crore before an economic NCI adjustment. This equals 47.845 times reported group PAT, 19.316 times operating EBITDA and 21.268 times FX-neutral EBITDA. P/E uses filed profit because owner PAT is unreconciled, not because it is accepted normalized earnings. Negative book NCI is never added as cash. Terminal NCI is an economic claim estimated from operating EV; subsidiary net debt/cash attribution is ND, so the proxy is not an assured conservative bound. Zero and 35%-of-group EBITDA allocation sensitivities are included. EV/EBITDA is useful for the capacity ramp but must be accompanied by capex, working capital and debt. No DCF with fabricated stable cash flow or matched-peer fair multiple is claimed. [S1,S16;E11]

The reproducible annual model uses commercial revenue paths for FY27–FY32 of Bear 112/112/118/125/132/139, Base 145/175/201/225/245/265, and Bull 185/230/270/310/345/380, all ₹ crore. EBITDA margin paths are Bear 14/14/15/15/15/15%, Base 20/21/22/22/22/22%, Bull 23/24/25/25/25/25%. Closing operating WC ratios are 60/51/47%. Cash capex paths are 6/6/7/7/8/8, 8/9/10/11/12/13 and 12/14/17/20/24/27. Interest assumptions are 12/10.5/9.5%; tax is a consolidated 26% proxy, without immediate loss refunds. This does not establish legal transfer of tax losses between entities. A separate ring-fenced-loss stress adds tax cost if subsidiary PBT losses of ₹4.1941/2 crore persist in FY27/FY28; entity-level tax details are ND. Depreciation is an economic 10% of opening PPE proxy, not a detailed asset schedule. Opening cash is ₹0.0864 crore; FY27 current principal of ₹5.2899 crore is repaid and later amortization assumptions are disclosed. No additional uncommitted bank draw, IPO cash, merger proceeds or subsidiary-loan asset is inserted in reference cases. [model/results.json]

All reference paths have early funding gaps to a ₹1 crore buffer: Bear ₹17.9654 crore, Base ₹15.6693 crore, Bull ₹19.6228 crore. Interest-inclusive hypothetical new-debt bridges of ₹29.5414/18.0149/21.6749 crore are solved by bisection for modeled year-end cash tests only, not represented as available facilities or sufficient intra-year liquidity. Seasonality, drawing power and covenant timing are ND. Terminal EV/EBITDA of 7/11/15 times, less all external group debt, plus cash once and less 20% of an assumed subsidiary operating-EV share, gives unfunded diagnostic prices ₹48.39/292.09/645.45. Five-year annualized returns including 2% entry and exit friction are −24.74%/7.83%/26.36%. These are not funded targets. With the hypothetical minimum debt bridges, returns become −26.95%/7.57%/26.21%. A separate ₹20 crore equity raise at ₹120 with 5% issue cost explicitly dilutes shares and gives a conditional base return of 6.82%; no actual issue is assumed. R and IAS remain NS. [model/results.json]

At a 15% hurdle, fixed-base-financing algebra using 11 times EBITDA and 22% margin requires about ₹353.46 crore commercial revenue, 23.74% annualized growth from FY26 ₹108.31 crore over the actual 5.5525 years to the terminal date. The 12% and 18% hurdles require ₹309.63 and ₹402.11 crore. Management's approximately ₹350 crore revenue-capacity claim is not proof of funding or net consolidated output. Base 7-times multiple normalization gives a diagnostic return of −1.46%. Margin lower by 3 percentage points gives 3.68% and a ₹22.77 crore funding gap; collections slower by 30 days give a ₹30.05 crore gap; annual capex higher by ₹5 crore gives ₹25.54 crore. Complete two-way margin ±3 points versus 7/11/15-times exit sensitivities are included. Diagnostic entry prices of ₹139.54 at 15%, or ₹159.25/122.68 at 12%/18%, are unsupported-financing algebra, not buy prices. The exact five-year terminal is interpolated from FY31/FY32 rather than falsely calling five fiscal years five investment years. [model/results.json]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent-impairment risk: High. A credible linked path is delayed US customer releases or trade-related disruption, weaker sales while inventory/WIP remain high, continuing agri underutilization and depreciation, rising WC borrowing or conditional renewal, discounted parent equity financing to support the 80%-owned subsidiary, and multiple compression. This is different from temporary quoted volatility: weaker earning power and dilution can permanently damage common shareholders' claims. [S1,S6,S7]

The bear no-new-money diagnostic ends at ₹48.39 per share, 74.86% below the entry price before execution friction, with a ₹17.97 crore peak buffer deficit. A hypothetical debt bridge reduces terminal value further to ₹41.70 through interest and debt claims. The linked lower-margin, slower-collection, half-WC-withdrawal and 10% debtor noncollection stress needs ₹38.42 crore of buffer funding. In the base path, withdrawal of half the ₹18.58 crore WC borrowing alone gives a ₹24.24 crore gap; a 20% receivable cash loss gives ₹22.41 crore. These are conditional stresses, not claims that lenders have withdrawn, receivables are fraudulent or insolvency has occurred. [model/results.json]

Recovery would come from parent engineering profitability, productive equipment, customer repeat orders and collections, not negative book NCI or face-value intercompany loans. Forced-sale appraisals, security priority and liquidation recoveries are ND, so book PPE is not a price floor. The clean audit and 5.57-times reported interest coverage are positives, but do not establish forward liquidity. Fundamental failure conditions include substantially weaker programme conversion, permanently inadequate subsidiary returns, or an accounting correction materially reducing owner earnings/equity. Shareholders bear loss after secured creditors and other senior claims. [S1;E7,E11]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
With 20,499,600 unchanged shares, 5 times today's value means equity capitalization ₹1,973.0865 crore; 10 times means ₹3,946.173 crore. At an illustrative 25-times owner P/E, required owner PAT is ₹78.9235/157.8469 crore. At a 10% owner PAT margin, required sales are ₹789.235/1,578.469 crore: roughly 7/14 times current reported group sales and well beyond the claimed ₹350 crore current revenue capacity. No-dilution is an assumption, not an entitlement. New equity increases aggregate profit needed for the same per-share return. [S1,S6,S16;model/results.json]

Required five-year price CAGRs are 37.97% and 58.49%; ten-year CAGRs 17.46% and 25.89%. Business growth need not equal price growth when multiples, margins and share count change. These outcomes would need additional customers and programmes, much better capital turnover and cash conversion, profitable agri operations, expansion beyond present capacity and consistent minority-claim accounting. Capitalizing the ₹470 crore nine-year order as a single year's sales would be wrong. Multiple expansion from approximately 48 times reported PAT is not a conservative engine of a fivefold outcome. [model/results.json]

Judgment: a long-duration entrepreneurial possibility, not a fundamentally supported five-year base case. Current evidence does not establish the funded reinvestment runway, unit returns or owner-earnings quality needed to validate either outcome. This is a scale-and-funding test, not a probability estimate or price target. [E6,E9,E11]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First reopening condition: obtain an issuer/auditor consolidation rollforward reconciling FY25/FY26 PAT, retained-profit additions, subsidiary losses, NCI, goodwill and EPS, including ownership history and intercompany entries. A complete explanation without economic impairment could remove G2 Hold. A material restatement requires all factors and valuation inputs to be revisited. Another clean opinion without the bridge is insufficient. [S1,S6]

At the first FY27 half-year filing, compare actual US programme billings and collections with management's approximately ₹60 crore annual run-rate expectation. Report the parent and 80%-owned subsidiary separately, then reconcile consolidated eliminations. Actual collections matter more than production announcements or RFQs. Watch new programme concentration and continuity of the largest customers. Disclosed cancellation or payment delay triggers BAL and D review. [S6,S10]

Funding evidence required before implementation: current cash/FD encumbrances, total and unused bank limits, drawing power, expiry, covenants, debt amortization and promoter-loan terms. Compare committed liquidity with the dated model gap, not with ₹35/25 crore intercompany authorization ceilings. Any new equity enters both cash and diluted share count. Any acquisition enters consideration, consolidation, WC, capex and NCI exactly once. [S1,S6]

Half-year operating checks: inventory growth versus commercial sales, DSO/ageing, actual GST/duty collections, sustained CFO conversion, agri break-even and cash returns after maintenance capex. Analytical alerts, not issuer guidance, include closing DSO above 130 days, inventory above 25% of commercial revenue, cash below confirmed next-year debt service without committed limits, or two further reporting periods of profit without operating cash. Recalculate CAP with multi-year cohorts when evidence permits. [S1;model/results.json]

Before any trade, verify the eligible exchange line, lot, corporate actions, ASM/GSM or trade-to-trade restrictions, actual spread and whole-lot depth. Replace the 59-row secondary history with complete official 60-session data, including verified no-print days. Liquidity must be recalculated for the actual intended size. This research has placed no orders, broker instructions, external outreach or monitoring automation. [S14–S18]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Watchlist with material financial-reliability and funding holds. It is not yet rankable as a compounder or investment candidate. BQS NS at 88% coverage, bounds 4.36–5.44; GQS NS at 85%, bounds 4.75–6.10; IAS NS at 40%, canonical bounds 1.80–7.20 and nested bounds 2.64–6.06. Overall confidence Low, forecast uncertainty High. GOV 4 is not an “Avoid for fraud” finding; G3 Hold is not observed funding failure. Missing CAP makes quality aggregates incomplete; G2 independently prevents ranking because it affects core consolidated capital and owner earnings. Funding Hold alone is not the reason. [E4,E6;model/score_audit.txt]

Existing manufacturing capability, a commercial US programme and profitable parent operations justify retaining the record. At this entry price, the burden of proof is on conversion of capex and orders into owner profit and cash. Reopen after consolidation reconciliation, current financing coverage and programme collections, then rebuild return/R/L with updated price and share count. A lower price alone cannot fix unreliable accounts or create bank headroom. Merger discussion, a new headline order or promoter optimism earns no separate bonus. [S1,S6,S9]

The ₹5 lakh reference cannot be implemented exactly. The verified 1,200-share lot costs ₹2.31 lakh at ₹192.50; two lots cost ₹4.62 lakh and three ₹6.93 lakh. Continuous 5%-participation capacity suggests 3.82–4.04 sessions but ignores block sizes. Only 9 of 59 observed sessions traded at least 24,000 shares, enough for one full lot at 5%. Known capacity of 11 lots across the 60-session calendar gives a two-lot equivalent of 10.91 sessions; historical completed-start median wait is 11, maximum 31, with 11 right-censored starts. These are observations under a missing-day treatment, not a promise. At 2%, one known lot across the window cannot complete two lots. At 10%, 53 known lots imply roughly 2.26 sessions but greater impact. This supports the explicit L 3 conditional downgrade. Suitability and position sizing are outside this dossier. [S14–S18;model/results.json]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Evidence hierarchy: issuer annuals and statutory filings, then the SEBI-hosted prospectus; management calls/presentations are marked as claims. The official interoperable exchange master and codebook establish lot/identity. Secondary dated OHLCV is used because the BSE bhavcopy route failed. Peer annual/product pages are primary qualitative comparators, not matched valuation evidence. Factor audits link to an evidence ledger recording scope, confidence and limitations. URLs, local hashes and page/section locators are preserved. Cutoff 20 October is separate from retrieval 21 October; later information is not backfilled. [S1–S24]

Access limitations: initial direct Python requests returned 403; public issuer PDFs were successfully retrieved via ordinary curl/public web and key pages visually sampled. Uppercase and lowercase BSE 19 October bhavcopy ZIP requests returned AccessDenied HTML, not data. An attempted REG1_IND191026 restriction file did not provide a valid issuer record; absence is not restriction clearance. The exact ISIN has an eligible SM row and an ineligible ST row in the master. They are not interchangeable. The secondary 60-session window lacks 25 August 2026; missing is not a verified zero. [S14–S18]

Actual turnover is bounded by daily low/high multiplied by share volume, rather than falsely calling close-times-volume reported exchange turnover. Allowing the missing day anywhere from zero to unbounded turnover leaves the 60-day mean upper bound ND, but conservative min(mean, median) capacity remains bounded at ₹24.7764–26.1720 lakh a day. Observed 20-session close-times-volume mean/median are ₹36.7627/27.6810 lakh. Observed 59-row mean/median are ₹30.8964/25.3506 lakh, not exact 60-session exchange values. Live bid-ask spread, full current BSE surveillance and latest shareholding/pledge clearance remain ND. [S14–S18;model/results.json]

Open questions with decision impact: consolidated goodwill/NCI/reserves/EPS; unused committed bank headroom and renewals; signed US programme terms and ultimate-customer concentration; agri unit economics and intercompany pricing; maintenance capex and asset-life cohorts; GST final disposal; current complete IPO utilization; FY27 collections; and terms of any future group transaction. Comparable three/five-year group CFO/PAT and ten-year revenue CAGR are ND, not zero. Acquisition-history precision and complete volume/currency attribution are also gaps. [S1,S6,S12,S23,S24]

Analyst assumptions are separately labeled: tax 26%, capital cost 11–14%, margin/capex/WC/interest paths, ₹1 crore buffer, exit multiples 7/11/15, an economic NCI proxy and 2% entry/exit friction. There are no scenario probabilities or assumed rescue. IPO cash, acquisitions, intercompany assets and guarantees are not double counted; no dividend is added while retaining the same terminal cash. Hypothetical debt/equity bridges are not facts. Canonical JSON, scripts, annual outputs, source ledger, access limitations, manifest and QA accompany the full dossier. Framework arithmetic is exact before half-up one-decimal display. [model/results.json]
